projects.title: LiDAR Odometry & SLAM Stack
projects.mainDescr: LiDAR odometry in C++ on KITTI: KISS-ICP-style scan-to-map registration, scored against ground truth and replayed live in an Open3D viewer.
projects.description: I'm building this C++ pipeline to behave like a real sensor stack rather than a batch script. A producer thread replays KITTI LiDAR scans at their original timing into a fixed-size queue, so if the consumer falls behind, the reader waits instead of piling scans up in memory. Each scan is deskewed using velocities integrated from the OXTS data, then registered against a voxel hash map with KISS-ICP-style ICP: an adaptive correspondence threshold and Gauss-Newton updates, with the work split across a thread pool that stays alive between iterations. I score the trajectory against KITTI ground truth with relative pose error, plot the per-step translation and rotation error against the mean and RMSE in Python, and can watch a run in an Open3D viewer that shows the accumulated map, the raw scans or the dense map from several camera modes.

projects.title: 3D Scene Reconstruction
projects.mainDescr: My own NeRF in PyTorch, trained on the Blender LEGO scene. It scores 31.20 dB PSNR averaged over all 200 test views, trained in fp32 on a 6 GB laptop GPU.
projects.description: Two ways of getting 3D out of 2D images. The first is a Structure-from-Motion pipeline that recovers camera poses and 3D points from ordinary photos: SIFT features, RANSAC, the fundamental and essential matrices, pose recovery, triangulation, PnP and bundle adjustment. The second is NeRF, which I implemented in PyTorch and trained on the synthetic LEGO scene to render it from new viewpoints. The current model reaches 31.20 dB PSNR and 0.9615 SSIM averaged over all 200 test views. It trained for 200,000 steps (about seven and a half hours) on my laptop's RTX 3060, all in fp32.

projects.title: KITTI Semantic Segmentation
projects.mainDescr: A UNet I wrote in PyTorch and trained from scratch on 160 KITTI images. It gets 0.400 mIoU over the 19 Cityscapes classes on 40 held-out images.
projects.description: Semantic segmentation of KITTI street scenes with a UNet I wrote from scratch in PyTorch. The first version trained on all 34 KITTI label IDs with the images squashed to 256×512. For the second one I switched to the 19 classes that are actually scored, kept KITTI's wide image shape (352×1184) with random scaling and crops, and used AdamW with warm-up and a poly learning-rate decay. I also wrote an evaluation script that scores a checkpoint the standard way, with one confusion matrix over the whole validation set. On 40 held-out images the last v2 checkpoint gets 0.400 mIoU, up from 0.364 for v1 scored the same way. Training v2 for 600 epochs took about four and a half hours on my laptop's RTX 3060.

projects.title: One-Shot Object Detection
projects.mainDescr: Training YOLOv5n, YOLOv5s, YOLOv5m and YOLOv5l on a basketball image dataset I put together, and comparing them.
projects.description: I trained four sizes of YOLOv5 (n, s, m and l) on a basketball image dataset I put together, and compared them across several train/test splits. The target is more than 85% average precision with the smallest one, YOLOv5n, on basketball video with several objects in frame and busy backgrounds.

projects.title: Hybrid A*
projects.mainDescr: A small Hybrid A* planner for ROS 2 that finds smooth, collision-free paths a car can actually drive. The planner is C++ and the visualization is Python.
projects.description: A Hybrid A* planning package for ROS 2 Humble. One node publishes an occupancy map along with the start and goal poses. The C++ planner searches over position and heading using forward and reverse motion primitives, guided by a heuristic, and smooths the resulting path so it stays within the car's turning limits. A Python node then animates the planned path.

projects.title: Trajectory Generation in Frenet Frame
projects.mainDescr: Samples lateral and longitudinal polynomial paths in the Frenet frame, scores them and picks a collision-free one in real time. Everything is drawn with OpenCV and saved to video.
projects.description: Trajectory planning in the Frenet frame, in C++. I build a reference path along the lane centre (x, y, yaw, curvature and arc length), then generate candidate trajectories: quintic polynomials for the lateral motion and quartic or quintic ones for the longitudinal motion, over several time horizons. Each candidate is scored on jerk, time and deviation from the centre line, and any that collide or break the kinematic limits are thrown out. The best one is converted back to world coordinates, and OpenCV draws all the candidates plus the chosen path and writes the result to trajectory.mp4.

projects.title: EKF Localization
projects.mainDescr: An Extended Kalman Filter tracking a simulated 4D unicycle, drawn live in OpenCV with a covariance ellipse that shrinks as the estimate settles. It can also save the animation as an MP4.
projects.description: A C++ simulation for trying out an Extended Kalman Filter. The robot follows a three-part reference path (a sine wave, a straight run downwards, then a semicircle) while the program generates noisy odometry and position measurements, and the filter runs its predict and update steps in real time. The OpenCV view rescales itself to keep everything in frame and colour-codes the ground truth, odometry, observations and EKF estimate. A red covariance ellipse shrinks as the uncertainty drops. The animation can optionally be recorded to ekf_demo.mp4.

projects.title: Atari Breakout DQN Agent
projects.mainDescr: A Deep Q-Network (DQN) that learns to play Atari Breakout, trained with Stable-Baselines3 using frame stacking and my own preprocessing.
projects.description: I wrapped the Breakout-v5 Gym environment with my own preprocessing (grayscale frames, frame skipping and a stack of the last four frames) and trained a Stable-Baselines3 DQN agent on it for 20 million timesteps on a GPU, tuning the hyperparameters along the way. An EvalCallback tracks progress and saves the best checkpoint during training, and Gym's RecordVideo wrapper records gameplay, so the videos show how the agent's play improves and what the final policy does.

projects.title: Sliding Mode Control for Quadrotor
projects.mainDescr: A sliding mode controller that makes a Crazyflie 2.0 track 3D polynomial trajectories in a Gazebo simulation.
projects.description: I designed a sliding mode controller for a Crazyflie 2.0 quadrotor so it can follow 3D polynomial trajectories in Gazebo despite the nonlinear dynamics and external disturbances. The trajectories are 5th-order polynomials, and a control allocation matrix turns the controller output into rotor speeds, which are published to Gazebo in real time. The SMC gains are exposed as tuning parameters. Flight data is logged during each run, and a separate script plots the actual trajectory in 3D.

projects.title: Travelling Salesman Problem
projects.mainDescr: Python algorithms for the Travelling Salesman Problem, with a live plot of the route and an MP4 of the search.
projects.description: A genetic algorithm in Python that finds short tours for the Travelling Salesman Problem. The first population is seeded with a greedy tour, and each generation uses elitism, roulette-wheel selection, ordered crossover and distance-based mutation. The parameters are easy to change. While it runs, Matplotlib shows the best route so far, and at the end it saves an MP4 of the route improving over the generations.

projects.title: Joint Space Control of SCARA Arm
projects.mainDescr: PID joint-space control for a SCARA arm in ROS, with an inverse kinematics solver that turns target positions into joint values.
projects.description: Joint-space control for a SCARA manipulator in ROS. An inverse kinematics solver works out the joint values for a target position, and a PID controller drives each joint there. The code is split into ROS packages with service servers, publishers and subscribers, and the arm's motion and joint trajectories are plotted live.

projects.title: Face Recognition/Verification Using Siamese Network
projects.mainDescr: A face recognition system built around a Siamese network in TensorFlow.
projects.description: Face recognition and verification with a Siamese network in TensorFlow, reaching at least 85% accuracy. I also implemented Google's FaceNet and a pre-trained random forest classifier to compare their accuracy with the Siamese network.

projects.title: Automatic Camera Calibration
projects.mainDescr: Camera calibration written from scratch in Python using Zhang's method: checkerboard detection, intrinsic and extrinsic estimation, and bundle adjustment.
projects.description: I wrote camera calibration from scratch in Python using Zhang's method. It detects the checkerboard corners, estimates a homography for each image, solves for the intrinsic and extrinsic parameters, models radial distortion and then refines everything with nonlinear bundle adjustment. I made plots to check each step and compared the final calibration with OpenCV's, getting sub-pixel reprojection error.
